historical_references.reference: According to Slavic legend, Jovana was a Princess of Serbia in the 13th century, who was renowned for her exceptional beauty. She was said to be the daughter of Prince Lazar Hrebeljanović and his wife Milica, and was married to Vukasin Mrnjavčević. Tragically, both Jovana and her husband were killed during the Battle of Kosovo in 1389.

Another reference for the name Jovana comes from the works of the 16th-century Croatian poet Marko Marulić. In his epic poem 'Judith', Jovana is depicted as a beautiful and pious woman, who is the wife of King Uldinus. She plays a significant role in the poem, as she uses her wisdom and charisma to persuade her husband to spare the life of the conquered city of Bethulia, which ultimately leads to the salvation of its inhabitants.
